newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, then ease.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, then ease.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Tuesday but quickly turned lower, under pressure from Wall Street's drop and strong resistance at the 2,600 level.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 2.40 points, or 0.09 percent, at 2,592.97 at 0930 GMT after opening at 2,599.73 -- its session high. The CAC-40 February futures contract was three points lower at 2,600.
Traders said the market was underpinned by firmness in bond prices and in the dollar.
"The dollar is heading towards 5.65 francs, the Matif is at a new historic high. There are only positive factors and that explains why the market is holding up well," said a trader.
Volume at 0945 GMT was 1.12 billion francs
Dassault Systemes shares were up 7.59 percent at 326 francs after the firm reported a rise in 1996 net income to 342.5 million francs from 221.3 million.
Insurer AGF shares were up 3.61 percent at 186.50 francs on speculation fuelled by an article in the newspaper La Tribune that suggested Allianz might be interested in a takeover bid.
